sn12.48:1.2: “Cosmology” (_lokāyata_) was a branch of worldly knowledge within regular Vedic studies concerned with the nature and extent of the world and how this may be known ([an9.38](), [sn12.48](); cf. Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.3.1). Vedic metaphysics posited “existence” as a primordial “oneness” from which the diversity of the world arises.
sn12.48:2.2: The “oldest cosmology” is a reference to the literal oldest Indian cosmology, Rig Veda 10.129.1, which begins: “The nonexistent did not exist, nor did the existent exist at that time” (Jamison/Brereton translation).
sn12.48:4.2: After discussing existence for six lines, the seventh begins, “That One breathed without wind by its independent will. There existed nothing else beyond that.” Then, ”that One was born by the power of heat”.
sn12.48:5.1: _Puthutta_ is used elsewhere of a “spreading” poison, but only here in a philosophical sense. Throughout the Rig Veda it is used for the “broad” earth or waters, spread out by the gods and burned over by Agni. It has sexual connotations, too: a capacious womb or a fat ass (10.86.8).
